sections.title: Letter xis sound
paragraphs: The letter name is (xis) /ʃis/. Its main sound is heard in (xadrez) /ʃɐˈdɾeʃ/, which means chess. This letter has four different sounds across words.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs: For the first sound, place your tongue just behind the tooth ridge. Push air through the gap with no voice. For the second, put your tongue tip on the tooth ridge. Push air while your voice hums. For the third, keep the same spot but turn the voice off. For the fourth, stop air at the back roof, burst it, then hiss immediately. Touch your throat to feel when the voice turns on.

sections.title: Spelling rules
paragraphs: At the start of a word, you hear the first sound, as in (caixa) /ˈkaj.ʃɐ/. After the opening letters ex before a vowel, it sounds like (exame) /iˈzɐ.mɨ/ or (exemplo) /iˈzẽ.plu/. In some classical words between vowels, it sounds like (próximo) /ˈpɾɔ.si.mu/ or (trouxe) /ˈtɾow.sɨ/. In learned words, it makes two sounds together, heard in (táxi) /ˈta.ksi/ and (fixo) /ˈfi.ksu/.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not always say this letter like the sound in the English word box. The most common Portuguese sound is like the sh in ship. When you see this letter at the start of a word, round your lips slightly and hiss smoothly without a k sound first.
